questions.title: Finding the Mode and Median of an Odd Ordered List

parts.text:
A student records the number of books read by 9 pupils in a term:
$$5,\; 7,\; 8,\; 8,\; 10,\; 12,\; 12,\; 12,\; 15$$
State the mode and determine the median of these values.

questions.title: Median of an Even Number of Ordered Values

parts.text:
The ordered test scores of 8 candidates are:
$$24,\; 28,\; 31,\; 35,\; 41,\; 44,\; 48,\; 52$$
Find the median test score.

questions.title: Quartiles and IQR for an Odd Sample Size

parts.text:
The ordered travel times in minutes for 11 workers are:
$$12,\; 15,\; 17,\; 18,\; 21,\; 24,\; 27,\; 30,\; 33,\; 36,\; 39$$
Given that the median is $24$, state the lower quartile $Q_1$ and calculate the interquartile range (IQR).

questions.title: Quartiles for an Even-Sized Ordered Data Set

parts.text:
An ordered list of 10 measurements is:
$$11,\; 13,\; 15,\; 18,\; 20,\; 22,\; 25,\; 27,\; 31,\; 36$$
Find the lower quartile $Q_1$ and upper quartile $Q_3$, and hence state the IQR.

questions.title: Identifying Quartile Classes in Grouped Data

parts.text:
A grouped frequency table has total frequency $N = 80$. The cumulative frequency for class $0 \le t < 10$ is $8$, and for class $10 \le t < 20$ is $25$.
State the target position for the lower quartile $Q_1$ and identify the class interval containing $Q_1$.

questions.title: Resistance of Median and IQR to Extreme Outliers

parts.text: A dataset consisting of $9$ values has median $5$ and interquartile range $5$. If the largest value is increased from $9$ to $90$, state the new median and explain why the interquartile range remains unchanged.

questions.title: Decimals and Median/IQR from Ordered Observations

parts.text:
A chemistry student measures the mass, in grams, of 11 chemical samples. The ordered values are:
$$0.214,\; 0.218,\; 0.221,\; 0.224,\; 0.229,\; 0.231,\; 0.235,\; 0.238,\; 0.242,\; 0.247,\; 0.251$$
Find the median mass.
For the same 11 measurements, find the lower quartile $Q_1$, the upper quartile $Q_3$, and the interquartile range.

questions.title: Quartile Class Intervals in a Grouped Frequency Distribution

parts.text:
The table shows the distribution of scores of 80 students in a competition:

$$\begin{array}{|c|c|c|}\hline \text{Score class} & \text{Frequency} & \text{Cumulative Frequency} \\ \hline 0 \le x < 10 & 7 & 7 \\ 10 \le x < 20 & 15 & 22 \\ 20 \le x < 30 & 25 & 47 \\ 30 \le x < 40 & 21 & 68 \\ 40 \le x < 50 & 12 & 80 \\ \hline \end{array}$$

Identify the class intervals containing the median and the upper quartile $Q_3$.

A student claims that the maximum possible value of the median is $30$ and the minimum possible value of $Q_1$ is $10$.
Evaluate these two bounds, and state the maximum possible difference between the median and $Q_1$ for this grouped data.

questions.title: Ordered Raw Data: Mode, Five-Number Summary, and Outlier Check

parts.text:
The numbers of hours worked per week by 15 part-time employees are:
$$6,\; 8,\; 10,\; 10,\; 12,\; 14,\; 15,\; 16,\; 18,\; 20,\; 20,\; 22,\; 25,\; 28,\; 45$$
Find the median and the interquartile range.

An outlier is defined as any value lying more than $1.5 \times \text{IQR}$ below $Q_1$ or more than $1.5 \times \text{IQR}$ above $Q_3$.
Show that $45$ is an outlier, and determine whether there are any low outliers.

questions.title: Greatest and Least Possible IQR in Grouped Integer Data

parts.text:
A survey of $100$ workers records their commuting expenses in integer dollars:

$$\begin{array}{|c|c|c|}\hline \text{Expense (dollars)} & \text{Frequency} & \text{Cumulative Frequency} \\ \hline 0 - 9 & 12 & 12 \\ 10 - 19 & 18 & 30 \\ 20 - 29 & 34 & 64 \\ 30 - 39 & 24 & 88 \\ 40 - 49 & 12 & 100 \\ \hline \end{array}$$

Identify the class intervals containing $Q_1$ and $Q_3$, showing clearly the target cumulative frequency positions.

Given that all data values are integers, find:
(i) the greatest possible value of the interquartile range,
(ii) the least possible value of the interquartile range.

questions.title: Quartiles and IQR from a Stem-and-Leaf Diagram

parts.text:
The stem-and-leaf diagram represents the waiting times, in minutes, of 16 patients at a clinic:

$$\begin{array}{r|llllllll} 1 & 2 & 4 & 5 & 8 \\ 2 & 1 & 3 & 6 & 7 & 9 \\ 3 & 0 & 2 & 5 & 8 \\ 4 & 1 & 4 & 6 \end{array}$$
$$\text{Key: } 2 \mid 3 \text{ represents } 23\text{ minutes}$$

Find the median waiting time and the mode.
For the same 16 waiting times, find the lower quartile $Q_1$, the upper quartile $Q_3$, and hence determine the interquartile range.

questions.title: Continuous Grouped Data: Cumulative Frequency, Linear Interpolation, and Boundary Extremes

parts.text:
The lifetimes, $t$ hours, of 120 electronic components are grouped as follows:

$$\begin{array}{|c|c|}\hline \text{Lifetime } (t \text{ hours}) & \text{Frequency} \\ \hline 0 \le t < 100 & 18 \\ 100 \le t < 200 & 32 \\ 200 \le t < 300 & 42 \\ 300 \le t < 400 & 20 \\ 400 \le t < 500 & 8 \\ \hline \end{array}$$

Construct a cumulative frequency column and identify the class intervals containing the median and the lower quartile $Q_1$.
Using linear interpolation within the respective class intervals, estimate the value of $Q_1$ and the median lifetime.

Given that $Q_3$ lies in the class $200 \le t < 300$ (target $CF = 90$):
(i) estimate $Q_3$ by linear interpolation and calculate the estimated IQR,
(ii) determine the greatest possible value that the interquartile range could theoretically take from the class boundaries.

questions.title: Comprehensive Data Comparison: Skewness, Outlier Resistance, and Distribution Spread

parts.text:
Two machines, $A$ and $B$, produce metal rods. The lengths (in mm) produced by Machine $A$ have the five-number summary:
$$\text{Minimum} = 42,\; Q_1 = 48,\; \text{Median} = 54,\; Q_3 = 62,\; \text{Maximum} = 95$$
(i) Calculate the interquartile range for Machine $A$.
(ii) Determine whether the maximum length ($95\text{ mm}$) is an outlier.
For Machine $A$, explain whether the distribution of rod lengths appears symmetrical, positively skewed, or negatively skewed, using both quartile differences and the presence of the extreme value.

Machine $B$ produces rods with median $53\text{ mm}$ and $\text{IQR} = 8\text{ mm}$. The mean length for Machine $A$ is $57.2\text{ mm}$ and the standard deviation is $11.4\text{ mm}$.
(i) State why the median and IQR are more appropriate than the mean and standard deviation for comparing the typical output and spread of these two machines.
(ii) Compare the performance of Machine $A$ and Machine $B$ in terms of central tendency and consistency.
